reuse.why: Most sites route through getScheduledAmount, but the helper re-derives the 7.5% tolerance instead of calling getApproxNumberThreshold from #shared/rules, and the API's expectedAmount ignores getScheduledAmount entirely.

duplication.why: scheduleModel.toExternal carries its own inline missing/number/range dispatch (with the stale furthest-from-zero rule and no isapprox handling), and the tolerance formula duplicates getApproxNumberThreshold.

placement.why: The rule correctly lives in shared/schedules.ts, but the API model embeds a second copy of the expected-amount rule in the API layer.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the amount rule, its callers, the API field and tests; the Omit<..., 'expectedAmount'> type churn is a necessary consequence.

maintainability.why: The API expectedAmount has already drifted from the shared rule (it still returns the end furthest from zero and treats approx as exact), exactly the divergence a maintainer would have to keep chasing.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal computes expectedAmount inline instead of getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount, false, schedule._amountOp); shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount reimplements getApproxNumberThreshold

disguised_duplication.where: api-models.ts expectedAmount nested ternary reshapes the getScheduledAmount dispatch (abs comparison instead of the helper); getScheduledAmount's Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) is getApproxNumberThreshold inlined

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an amountOp parameter (replacing roundSumBeforeDividing) and an isapprox branch; scheduleModel.toExternal bypasses it with its own range rule
